name: Bluetooth LE advertising
label: Bluetooth LE
notes: Bluetooth Low Energy advertising (LE 1M PHY, GFSK), decoded by OnAir's receiver through the onair-rx handler; the row has no decoder of its own, so only a handler runs it. One job reads one advertising channel: start it on 2402, 2426 or 2480 MHz (channels 37, 38 and 39) with a band of 2 MHz; the handler takes 4 MHz of IQ (OnAir's own minimum, a decimation to 4 samples a bit), so the node resamples to it. Each event is a good advertising packet naming a device: `mac` (the advertiser's address, or the scanner's for a scan or connection request; lower-case hex without separators), `name` (the packet's own name, null when it has none: a device names itself in some of its packets only) and `rssi_db` (the packet's level in dB below full scale, not calibrated). Advertising only: connections are not followed and nothing is decrypted; the packets (the access address, the dewhitened PDU and its CRC, link type 251) go to a packet capture, an extended advertisement, which names no device, among them. Ranges and bands: the three advertising channels at 2402, 2426 and 2480 MHz and the 2400 to 2483.5 MHz ISM band are the Bluetooth Core Specification's (LE advertising channels 37, 38 and 39); identify and classify try the row anywhere in that band, and a job started by hand runs anywhere. Listing bar: measured on the build host (12 cores) through a scratch node's release build, 30 s of the generated capture looping on a file source and fed in real time; the job skipped no input, onair-rx used 0.15 of a core and the node 0.29 of a core (load average 12.2 to 8.2, with another build running).
